title: Annotatio IV §.XVII: Waldensian Confession — true body and blood by faith; bread and wine substance unchanged
pass_a_gloss: At last Morneus subjoins: Let the Waldenses’ Confession make faith, which let the Reader not disdain to consult, since nearly all the Transubstantiators’ arguments are there refuted solidly enough for the time. The Sum is: In the Sacred Supper celebrated according to Christ’s Institution, the faithful receives the true body and blood of Christ: Meanwhile the nature or substance of bread or wine is by no means changed, for Christ’s words induce no Conversion; And if the Element should cease, there would no longer be a Sacrament.
pass_b_english: Morneus: consult the Waldensian Confession — it solidly answers most Transubstantiators’ arguments for its time.

Sum: in the Supper per Christ’s Institution the faithful receives Christ’s true body and blood; bread and wine nature/substance are not changed — His words induce no Conversion; if the element ceased, there would be no Sacrament.
source_text: Tandem subjicit Mornæus: Waldensium Confessio fidem faciat, quam consulere Lector ne dedignetur, quandoquidem omnia ferè Transsubstantiatorum argumenta solidè satis, pro tempore, ibi refutantur. Summa est: In S. Cœna secundum Institutionem Christi celebrata, fidelem, verum Christi corpus & sanguinem accipere: Panis interim aut vini naturam aut substantiam minimè mutari, verba enim Christi nullam Conversionem inducere; Et, si Elementum desineret, Sacramentum non ampliùs fore.
